questions.q: How does ISO 27001 fundamentally differ from SOC 2 in what it produces?
options: ISO 27001 results in a certification of a management system; SOC 2 produces an attestation report on controls
ISO 27001 only applies to software companies, while SOC 2 applies to all industries
They produce identical outputs and differ only in which country issues them
ISO 27001 is issued by the AICPA, the same body that issues SOC 2
questions.explain: ISO 27001 certifies that an organization's Information Security Management System meets the standard, issued by an accredited certification body. SOC 2 is a CPA firm's attestation report describing control design or operation.

questions.q: What is the ISMS that ISO 27001 actually certifies?
options: A single firewall configuration document
The organization's documented, risk-based system for identifying, treating, and continuously improving information security risk management
A list of every employee's password
A one-time penetration test report
questions.explain: The ISMS is the Plan-Do-Check-Act management system itself — risk assessment feeding decisions, decisions feeding controls, controls being monitored and feeding the next cycle — not a specific technical control.

questions.q: What is Annex A in ISO 27001?
options: A mandatory checklist every certified organization must fully implement with no exceptions
The legal contract between the organization and the certification body
A reference catalog of control objectives and controls an organization draws from based on its own risk assessment
A list of every past security incident the organization has had
questions.explain: Annex A (93 controls across 4 themes in the 2022 revision) is a catalog, not a mandatory checklist. Applicability is meant to be risk-driven — an organization selects from it based on its own risk assessment.

questions.q: What does the Statement of Applicability (SoA) record for each Annex A control?
options: Only whether the organization passed its last financial audit
The names of every employee who has access to that control
The exact dollar cost of implementing that control
Whether the control is applicable, whether it's implemented and how, or a documented justification if it's excluded
questions.explain: The SoA maps every Annex A control to applicable-and-implemented, applicable-with-a-reference, or not-applicable-with-an-explicit-justification — which is why due-diligence reviewers ask to see the SoA itself, not just the certificate.

questions.q: What happens between an ISO 27001 organization's Stage 2 audit and its recertification audit roughly three years later?
options: Nothing — certification is valid automatically for three years with no further review
The certification body re-issues Annex A with new controls every year
The organization must repeat the Stage 1 audit every month
Typically annual surveillance audits that confirm the ISMS is still functioning
questions.explain: Certification bodies typically run smaller-scope surveillance audits, often annually, between the initial Stage 2 certification and the full recertification audit roughly every three years.
